summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fatigue, malaise, low-grade fever, and loose stools. He has a history of HCV cirrhosis with ascites, portopulmonary hypertension on remodulin, and recent tunneled line replacement. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and stable bilateral lower lobe opacities on chest X-ray, but no focal infection source. Stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, Shigella, and Campylobacter. Paracentesis showed minimal PMNs, ruling out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. Blood cultures remained negative. His symptoms improved without antibiotics, supporting a viral gastroenteritis diagnosis. He underwent therapeutic paracentesis to remove 8 liters of ascites after platelet transfusion due to thrombocytopenia, with symptomatic relief. All home medications, including remodulin, were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight and follow up with his transplant team.
